channel.title: AGSIST Daily
channel.description: Free morning market briefing for grain and livestock farmers: overnight futures, USDA reports and the news behind the moves. Posted most days between 5:45 and 6:30 a.m. Central, by Sigurd Lindquist, CCA.

item.title: Hogs near $56 as pork cutout slips; export sales due 7:30
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: December hogs settled at $56.03 while the national cash hog price sat at $43.25. That gap is about $12.78 a hundredweight, and futures buyers are paying well over what packers paid on the kill. • Hogs: futures above cash • Grains: corn flat, beans soft • Cattle and crude Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-12

item.title: Corn slips 2½ cents to $4.46½ after Tuesday's yield cut
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Dec corn is at $4.46½ overnight, 2½ cents under Tuesday's $4.49 settle. A Farm Policy News item says USDA's yield cut was bigger than traders expected, and corn had its best day in three months. • Cattle up, cash hogs soft • Crude firms on Iran doubts Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-11

item.title: WASDE prints at 11 CT; Dec corn is at $4.41½ overnight
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: USDA's WASDE and Crop Production come out at 11:00 a.m. CT today. Dec corn closed Monday at $4.39¼, and the 11:00 a.m. CT USDA report is the first number that can move it. Overnight trade added only 2¼ cents, which is a small move for a report day. That's what a market standing still looks like. • Grains wait on USDA • Hogs bounce, cattle gain • Crude slips on Iran signal Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-10

item.title: Crude slips 2.9% to $88.18 as Trump signals no new Iran strikes
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: WTI crude is at $88.18 overnight, down 2.9% from Friday's $90.83 settle, after President Trump signaled no immediate plans for more attacks on Iran. Grains barely moved ahead of Crop Progress at 3:00 p.m. CT, with December corn at $4.43. • Crude slips on Iran signal • Grains flat before reports Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-09

item.title: Mexico's record corn sale and Monday's crop report lead the week
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: A reported record corn sale to Mexico lifted Dec corn to **$4.41½** Friday, a small bounce after a losing week. That is a few cents back on a bushel, not a turn in the trend. • Grains bounce, wheat slips • Hogs fall, cattle ease Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-08

item.title: Corn, beans and wheat all fell this week; hogs sank
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn and soybeans bounced a little Friday after a rough week of fund selling. Hogs did not bounce. December hogs closed at $53.525, down 2.9% and near the bottom of their 52-week range. • Corn and beans bounce, wheat slips • Hogs lead livestock lower Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-07

item.title: Hog futures fall 4.3% to $55.10; cattle slip 1.7% Thursday
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: December hogs settled Thursday at $55.10, down 4.3%, the biggest drop on the board. Live cattle slipped 1.7% to $214.40 and feeders lost 2.1%. With feeding losses at $328 a head, a falling board squeezes feeders and packers both. • Hogs and cattle fall • Grains hold steady, wheat lower Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-06

item.title: Midterms hand Democrats Congress; Dec corn is at $4.47¼ overnight
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Democrats took Congress with wins in farm states, but December corn barely moved overnight at $4.47¼. Nobody is pricing the farm bill yet. Today's corn price still comes from harvest supply and export demand. • Grains edge up before export sales • Cattle flat, hogs soft • Crude firms as Hormuz fires continue Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-05

item.title: Soybeans fall to new lows; four tankers hit mines near Hormuz
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Jan soybeans are at $12.03¼ overnight, down 10¾ cents from Tuesday's $12.14 settle, a fresh low for this slide. Four oil tankers hit mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said, and WTI is still $95.38. • Beans make new lows • Cattle slip, hogs edge up • Crude holds near $95 Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-04

item.title: Dec corn trades at $4.44½ Tuesday morning, under Monday's $4.48¼ settle
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Dec corn is at $4.44½, 3¾ cents under Monday's settle, with harvest 74% done. That is a quiet slide, but it means the bushels still in the field have not changed the price picture yet. • Corn and beans edge lower • Cattle dip, hogs stay low Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-03

item.title: Crude drops 4.6% to $99.38; cattle futures fell Friday
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Crude fell 4.6% to **$99.38** on hopes for a US-Iran peace deal, which lets the harvest diesel bill ease for now. Cattle already gave back 2.4% Friday, so a feeder buyer is paying less than a week ago. • Crude slides on Iran talk • Cattle futures fall hard Friday • Grains edge up Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-02

item.title: Corn ends the week at $4.47¾; crude up 2.1% to $104.12
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: December corn settled Friday at $4.47¾, down 3½ cents, its second lower close in a row, while beans held near $12.22. Corn is giving ground with harvest running and soybeans steady, so the feed side of the ledger got cheaper this week. • Grains end the week soft • Cattle and hogs slip • Crude stays high Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-11-01

item.title: Corn ends the week at $4.47¾; crude up 2.1% to $104.12
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: December corn closed Friday at $4.47¾, down 3½ cents, its second lower close in a row. Beans added 2½ cents to $12.22¼, so corn lost a little ground to beans on the week. Crude ended at $104.12, up 2.1%, which keeps diesel costs firm while corn sits near its harvest lows. • Grains close the week soft • Cattle and hogs slip Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-31

item.title: Crude up 2.2% to $104.27 as Houthis hit Saudi sites
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Crude is up 2.2% to $104.27 after new Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites, while corn and beans barely moved. Diesel is the cost that is climbing for harvest hauling, and grain prices are not paying you for it. • Energy runs higher again • Grains hold harvest lows • Hogs bounce, cattle flat Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-30

item.title: Hogs fall 5.5% to $58.60 while corn holds $4.51
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Lean hogs settled Wednesday at $58.60, down 5.5% and the biggest drop on the board, only 1% off their 52-week low. Every hog sold this week brought less than it would have Tuesday. • Hogs lead the board lower • Grains drift on harvest • Crude eases on Iran talk Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-29

item.title: Corn bounces 2¾¢ to $4.51½ after four lower closes
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Dec corn is at $4.51½ overnight, up 2¾ cents from Tuesday's $4.48¾ settle. That ends a run of lower closes. Soybeans are at $12.33¼ overnight, up 4 cents, after two lower closes. A fast harvest has been the weight on grain, and one overnight bounce does not change that. • Grains bounce after a slide • Hogs fall, cattle hold • Crude firm, gas gains Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-28

item.title: Corn slips ½¢ to $4.54½ after three lower closes
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Dec corn is at $4.54½ overnight, ½ cent under Monday's settle, and has given back a few cents all week. Beans are up 7½ cents to $12.48¾ after Monday's drop. • Corn quiet, beans bounce • Crude firm, gas gains • Cattle firm, hogs lower Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-27

item.title: Corn dips 3¢ to $4.53, beans lose 16¢ to $12.40
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Soybeans gave back 16 cents overnight to $12.40, and meal fell harder at 1.8%, while corn barely moved at $4.53. Beans are carrying the grain market lower today. The 16 cents is a November futures move; what it means for beans in the bin depends on your local bid and basis. (Corrected Oct 27, see the note below.) • Beans lead grains lower • Cattle hold near highs • Crude slips; gas gains Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-26

item.title: Corn ends the week at $4.56; crude up 3.8% to $103
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn ended the week at **$4.56**, down 4½ cents, and soybeans edged up to $12.56½. Grains barely moved, but crude gained 3.8% to $103.27. That is the number that reaches your fuel and fertilizer bills next season, not the corn price. • Grains finish the week quiet • Cattle hold near highs • Crude gains; gas drops Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-25

item.title: Corn ends the week at $4.56 as crude gains 3.8% to $103
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed Friday at $4.56, down 4½ cents, while beans added 3½ cents to $12.56½. Crude ran the other way, up 3.8% to $103.27 as Saudi-Houthi tension pushed Brent toward $120. • Grains finish the week quiet • Cattle hold near highs • Crude climbs, gas drops Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-24

item.title: Corn slips 4½¢ to $4.56 as crude climbs 3.7% to $103
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed lower at $4.56, while crude jumped 3.7% to $103. Soybeans edged up to $12.57½. Grain is soft and fuel is firm, so a farmer's input bill is rising while the corn check is not. • Corn eases, beans edge up • Cattle hold near $230 • Crude and gas jump Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-23

item.title: Corn $4.64 and beans $12.47 hold; crude up 2.2% to $99.24
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is at $4.64 overnight, up three-quarters of a cent from Wednesday's $4.63¼ settle, after lower closes. Soybeans are at $12.47, up 1¾ cents, after eight straight lower closes. item.title: Corn settled lower 6 days straight, $4.62 on Oct 20; beans 7 days, $12.48¼
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Dec corn settled Tuesday at $4.62, its sixth lower settle in a row, and Nov soybeans settled at $12.48¼, their seventh; early Wednesday corn traded at $4.59½ and beans at $12.45. (Corrected Oct 27, see the note below.) item.title: Corn at $4.67¾ and beans at $12.57½ barely move after losing streaks
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn at $4.67¾ and soybeans at $12.57½ are both a few cents higher overnight, which is hardly a bounce after streaks of five and six lower closes. A farmer holding unpriced bushels is still looking at the lowest prices of the run. • Grains bounce after losing runs • Crude slips but stays above $100 Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-20

item.title: Crude down 3% to $98.41 on Trump-Putin diesel deal; grains flat
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Crude fell about $3 overnight to **$98.41** on word of a US-Russia deal that could add diesel supply. Corn at **$4.73** and beans at **$12.61** barely noticed. For harvest fuel bills, that is the first bit of relief in a while, though crude is still close to $100. • Crude slips on diesel deal • Grains hold flat • Cattle edged up Friday Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-19

item.title: Corn slips 3¾¢ to $4.74¼; crude gains 3.5% to $101
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn closed Friday at $4.74¼, down 3¾ cents, while soybeans held at $12.61¼ and wheat lost 9½ cents. Crude was the big mover, up 3.5% to $101.41 as Iran war supply worries carry into 2027. • Grains ease into the weekend • Cattle firm, packers in focus Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-18

item.title: Corn and beans break lower; crude tops $101 on tight supply
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn settled Friday at $4.74¼, down 3¾ cents, and beans closed at $12.61¼, off 1¾ cents, both pressured by harvest supply all week. item.title: Corn and beans break lower as harvest pressure builds
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is at $4.74¼ overnight, down 4 cents, and beans are off 3¾ cents at $12.60½. China bought more US beans this week, its first cargoes since the Trump-Xi summit, but harvest supply is still winning. Every bushel coming out of the field right now is being sold into a market that already has plenty. • Corn and beans break lower • Cattle firm, feeders hold • Crude holds near $99 on tanker risk Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-16

item.title: Grain holds steady overnight ahead of export sales report
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: Corn is trading at $4.80 overnight, barely off Wednesday's $4.80¾ settle. Beans sit at $12.73¼, down 4 cents, with weekly export sales due Thursday at 7:30 a.m. CT. Nothing has moved yet, so the board is sitting right where harvest left it. • Corn and beans wait on export sales • Cattle and hogs ease back slightly • Crude slips as Trump weighs easing tanker sanctions Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-15

item.title: Crude tops $95 on more tanker threats; grain holds steady
item.dc:creator: Sigurd Lindquist
item.description: WTI crude is at $95.36 overnight, up 1.3%, after Iran told Reuters its forces plan to intensify strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Corn and wheat drifted lower overnight while beans firmed to $12.90½. Diesel costs for fall fieldwork are the thing to watch, not the grain board. • Corn and wheat drift, beans firm • Crude pushes toward $95 on Hormuz threats Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-14
